wall.purpose: Page background in light mode; follows color-scheme.

wall-ink.purpose: Text painted directly on the wall.

wall-muted.purpose: Secondary text on the wall (header tagline).

enamel.purpose: Station sign plate; identical in both schemes.

board.purpose: Every board and the selected mode tab; text on status tiles.

board-edge.purpose: 1px board edges, row dividers, share-ticket top edge.

row.purpose: Answer rows, share ticket, summary cells.

tile-top.purpose: Upper half of a flap tile.

tile-bottom.purpose: Lower half of a flap tile; field and step-cell fill.

key-edge.purpose: Outline of keys, fields, answer rows and step cells.

well.purpose: Recessed trough behind switch tracks and the countdown.

ink-dim.purpose: Labels and secondary copy on boards.

signal.purpose: Marks "now" only: selected mode bar, lit step, current log row, your row, the one primary key, focused next code tile; also the keyboard focus ring.

signal-ink.purpose: Text on signal and on route badges.

line-blue.purpose: General, Sports and Vehicles; player line.

line-magenta.purpose: Entertainment and Celebrities; hard difficulty; player line.

line-teal.purpose: Science and Animals; easy difficulty; player line.

line-orange.purpose: History, Geography and Politics; medium difficulty; player line.

ok.purpose: Correct, always with a check glyph and a word.

bad.purpose: Wrong, timeout, errors and urgent countdown, always with a glyph and a word.

display.purpose: Name on the sign plate only; condensed caps.

flap.purpose: Split-flap readouts: question number, score, time, room code. Sizes md 20px, lg clamp(28px, 5vw, 36px), xl clamp(38px, 8vw, 56px), code tiles 34px.

question.purpose: Question text; sentence case, max 34em, never flips.

key.purpose: Keys and mode tabs, uppercase; primary key at 18px.

label.purpose: Field labels, readout labels, column heads, stat terms; uppercase, ink-dim.

shadows.name: board-on-wall
shadows.purpose: Every board, banner, the sign plate and the open picker: the only thing that casts onto the wall.

shadows.name: key-lip
shadows.purpose: Board keys, counter keys, kbd hints. Removed on press with a 1px sink.

shadows.name: sign-plate-rule
shadows.purpose: The painted rule inset on the enamel sign, combined with board-on-wall.

shadows.name: mode-sign
shadows.purpose: The sliding black plate with its yellow bar under the selected mode tab.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: The one curve for everything that travels.

motion.name: board-hang
motion.value: 520ms settle from perspective(1400px) translateY(-14px) rotateX(9deg), 70ms stagger (side rails 620ms, 90ms)
motion.purpose: Boards swing onto their hooks when a mode is shown.

motion.name: flap-cascade
motion.value: 55ms per drum step, 45ms stagger per tile, max 6 steps; leaf falls in 80ms cubic-bezier(0.55, 0, 1, 0.45)
motion.purpose: Codes, numbers and short labels flip to their new character. Question text never flips.

motion.name: stage-in
motion.value: 460ms settle, translateX(+/-28px) from the direction of travel
motion.purpose: A new question arrives from the side the player moved towards.

motion.name: row-in
motion.value: 420ms settle, translateY(10px) with clip reveal, 60ms per row after 110ms
motion.purpose: Answer rows and how-to lines arrive like departure lines.

motion.name: tile-turn
motion.purpose: The letter tile flips over to its result.

motion.name: route-flip
motion.purpose: The route badge flips in on change.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Leaves, hangs, slides and pulses are removed; every state change lands in place.

components.name: Step Row
components.description: One cell per question with a check, cross or pending mark; the lit cell is now.

narrative.overview:
Every quiz is a timetable. Questions, room codes and scores arrive on matte black split-flap boards hung on a station-hall wall. The wall is the page and follows the viewer's light or dark preference. The boards are always black, and the enamel station sign above them is the same painted off-white by day and by night. Each board is a separate module with a gap of wall between it and the next, and each hangs from its top edge and swings into place when its mode is shown.

The system is dense and mechanical without being noisy. Codes, numbers and short labels sit on flap tiles: two halves split by a hairline seam, each character flipping forward through a drum until it lands. Everything written to be read, like question text, answers and explanations, is set in a readable grotesk and never flips. One colour, signal yellow, marks what is happening now. Five line colours tell categories, difficulty levels and players apart, like route bullets on a real board. Correct and wrong always pair a drawn glyph with a word.

This world rejects the trivia-app default: a gradient card with coloured answer tiles. It has no blended gradients, no glows and no soft, heavily rounded SaaS cards.
keyCharacteristics: Black boards on a wall that follows the colour scheme; boards and sign plate do not change between schemes.
Split-flap tiles (a hard 50% split and a 1px seam) for codes, numbers, ranks and answer letters.
Five line colours, each always paired with a code, a pip count or a name.
Condensed caps for signage, readable sentence case for reading.
Controls read as physical keys, with a darker lip underneath that sinks 1px when pressed.
One settle curve for all motion; with reduced motion, things land in place instead of travelling.

rules.name: The Now Rule
rules.body: Signal yellow only marks "now": the selected mode's sign bar, the lit step cell, the current answer-log row, your leaderboard row, the one primary key per screen, and the focused next room-code tile. The yellow keyboard focus ring follows the same logic, because it marks where you are. Anything that is not "now", such as the share ticket's top edge, uses board-edge ink instead.

rules.name: The Line Rule
rules.body: A line colour is never the only signal. It always comes with a code (a route badge), a count (pips), or a name (the player or the line map entry).

rules.name: The Glyph-and-Word Rule
rules.body: Correct and wrong are always a drawn glyph plus a word, never colour alone.

rules.name: The Black Board Rule
rules.body: Only the wall follows `prefers-color-scheme`. Boards stay black and the sign plate stays enamel in both schemes.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Condensed caps are for signage, flaps, keys and labels. Sentence-case grotesk is for questions, answers and explanations. The two never swap roles.

rules.name: The Question Never Flips Rule
rules.body: Only codes, numbers and short labels use the flap cascade. Question and answer text arrives by sliding in, never character by character.

rules.name: The Hung Board Rule
rules.body: Only whole boards cast a shadow on the wall. Nothing inside a board floats. Depth there comes from lips, seams and wells.

dos: Do put every new screen on black boards hung on the wall, with separate modules, gaps of wall between them, and a 6px corner with the board-on-wall shadow.

Do keep signal yellow to the "now" list: the selected mode's sign bar, the lit step cell, the current answer-log row, your leaderboard row, the one primary key per screen, and the focused next room-code tile.
Do pair every line colour with a code, a pip count or a name.
Do show correct and wrong as a drawn glyph plus a word, in ok or bad.
Do set codes, numbers, ranks and letters on split-flap tiles (hard 50% split and 1px seam), and drop the seam when a tile lights up solid.
Do use condensed caps for signage, keys and labels, and the sentence-case grotesk for questions and answers.
Do move with the settle curve and give every animation a reduced-motion path that lands in place.
Do use the drawn 24px icon set (2px round strokes, currentColor).
donts: Don't use blended gradients or glows. The only gradient in the system is the hard 50% stop that draws a flap tile's two halves.
Don't use soft, heavily rounded SaaS cards; board corners stop at 6px.
Don't use signal yellow for decoration, celebration or share tickets.
Don't make boards or the sign plate follow the colour scheme; only the wall changes.
Don't flip question or answer text through the flap cascade.
Don't use a line colour on its own, or colour alone for correct and wrong.
